newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso closes soft on late dollar short cover.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso closes soft on late dollar short cover.

text.p: The Mexican peso relinquished earlier strength to close slightly weaker on Wednesday as dealers rushed to cover dollar positions in late trade, dealers said.
"Several banks had to buy dollars at the official central bank fixing rate, which softened the peso,' said a trader.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate both closed 0.35 of a centavo weaker, at 7.8610/7.8635 and 7.8525/7.8575 per dollar.
The peso had gained strength in early trade as foreign investors switched to peso investments, but the inflow of dollars was insufficient to meet late demand for cover, traders said.
The same-day peso closed 3.6 centavos firmer at 7.8310/7.8340 per dollar.
Dealers added that dollar short-covering prevented the peso from breaking resistance.
"There was definitely an inflow of dollars, but banks that were short when the central bank announced its fixing rate pulled the peso back from resistance at 7.83 per dollar," a tarder said.
The 48-hour peso stood at 7.8420/7.8460 per dollar at its firmest during the session.
